As shown in the figure, 4 million grids and 6 million grids showed almost
identical results. Based on the result, it was judged that the use of 4
million grids would be sufficient for the accuracy of the solution. For all
subsequent analysis, about 4 million grids were used..

Figs. 11–14 show the distributions of instantaneous temperature,
average temperature, instantaneous mass fraction of O2, and mean mass

fraction of O2 in the center plane of BI-AM02..

The temperature distributions in Figs. 11 and 12 were somewhat
over predicted because the chemical equilibrium combustion model was
applied.

From the results of the numerical analysis, the combustion pressure
and characteristic velocity were derived as time-averaged values, and
the maximum temperature of the pintle tip was obtained after the flame
was fully developed. The numerical analysis results are shown in
Table 4.

From the analysis results, the pintle tip temperature of A with heat
damage was highest at 1868 K and that of AI with the insert nozzle was
1468 K, resulting in a temperature difference of 400 K because of the
insert nozzle. In addition, the highest temperature for B ( _BF_ 58%) was
1545 K and that for BI with the insert was 1398 K, for a temperature
difference of 147 K. The pintle tip temperature was thus reduced by 323
K (17.3%) by changing the _BF_ from 86% to 58% and varied by 147 K
(9.5%) to 400 K (21.4%) depending on the insert nozzle.

Fig. 15 shows the streamline and flow velocity at the center plane of
the pintle injector. It is confirmed that the flow rates of injectors A and B
without the insert nozzles are low because the flow rate that goes out
directly to the orifice and that which exits after cooling the pintle tip are
not smooth. However, the pintle injectors with the insert nozzles
distribute the flow well, and the flows are smooth along the internal
curvature without flow velocity reductions towards the pintle orifice
exit. Therefore, it was experimentally confirmed that the pintle tip was
cooled effectively.

According to the numerical analysis results presented in Table 4, the
type A pintle injector was predicted to have a higher temperature at the
tip than the type B injector. The type B pintle injector (BF 58%) has a
higher flow rate than type A (BF 86%) through the orifice, which is
believed to play a role in pushing out the flames formed at the pintle tip.
Fig. 16 shows the temperature distribution at the pintle tip. From the
numerical analysis results, it was predicted that the type A injector
would have relatively lower thermal durability than the type B injector
and that the pintle tips of A and AI would be damaged in the actual
combustion test.

The characteristic velocity of type B was observed to be relatively
